fr.elements: Main Residence; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Landscaped Area; Landscaped Area; Open Green Space; Patio Area; Water Feature; Perimeter Fencing; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Multiple Structures
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders arriving under low-visibility conditions can identify it without delay.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow fire or medical apparatus to reach the main residence and detached structure without obstruction.
• Create a designated turnaround area near the main residence or detached structure so large emergency vehicles can reverse out without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the driveway so branches do not block the roof line of a fire engine or ambulance traveling to the structures.
• Cut back dense vegetation between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings on foot without obstruction.
• Keep a clear walking path between the main residence and the detached structure free of planters, water feature equipment, and landscape features that could slow foot movement at night.
• Thin dense plantings adjacent to the perimeter fencing so responders can identify gate locations quickly from inside and outside the property.
• Mark any gate in the perimeter fencing with a reflective indicator and keep it unlocked or secured with a standard break-away lock for emergency access.
• Keep the patio area clear of furniture and portable items that could block movement or staging during an emergency

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Green Space; Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Groups; Irrigated Landscape; Multiple Access Routes; Scattered Trees; Open Terrain; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree clusters nearest to the structure to reduce the amount of burnable material close to the building.
• Trim branches and shrubs that are directly touching or overhanging the structure.
• Separate individual scattered trees from nearby shrub groupings by removing shrubs growing directly beneath tree canopies.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from within the vegetation groups visible near the structure.
• Keep low-growing shrubs scattered across the property trimmed back and away from the building walls.
• Maintain the open green space areas by keeping grass mowed short during dry periods.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Maintain the open terrain between vegetation groups and the structure by preventing shrubs or small trees from filling in those gaps over time.
